When I had 6 kids under ten, there were A LOT of things that need cleaning. My first thought was Sams, buy that cleaner in bulk! And while it did cut overall costs, you have to have that kind of money up front to invest in those big bottles. Sometimes I really didn't so I went about finding different solutions.

I took a step back and looked at where my dollars were going and what /how much I really used on a bi weekly basis. I realized I used countless rolls of paper towels to clean with.... a habit given to me by my very OCD mother. She never wanted to touch dirty rags. I decided to try using rags instead of paper towels as my first step towards cutting that part of my budget. Now back when I made this switch microfiber clothes were not available so I bought a pack of bar towels from Sams. Ten dollars for a dozen. If it didn't work 'I could use them in the kitchen.

I brought them home cut half of them into fourths and started using them to clean everything. I put a bucket in the laundry to throw the used ones into, every two or three days I'd throw in the washer with some bleach and hot water. They scrubbed surfaces, they mopped- spills like a champ, glass surfaces could be scrubbed with a wet one and polished off with clean dry one. The bigger ones also double as dish towels and spot mopping with my foot. Another win was I was not filling our trash cans with paper towels, a little better for the environment in my world. But best of all in that one 10 dollar investment I saved almost 50 dollars over 6 months. If someone is working a minimum(ish) wage job that's between 10 and 15 hours of labor that you aren't spending on something that's used up quickly and has to be replaced.

Now there are microfiber clothes that are powerhouses of work. I buy them in two colors and cut them inn half. One color are just for use on the floors. They work great in the swifter holders, I sew them into steam mop pads. But that one color gets washed separately because I'm a bit OCD. The other color does all the cleaning from dusting to washing counters. Inside and outside window cleaning, these little boogers can get kid sticky, pet smeared windows sparkly clean with little effort. It's not much added work in the scheme of things. One or two more little loads of clothes. I did have a friend who put an old diaper pail to work, it had a lid and kept them out of her sight until wash time.

Think about that when you buy house cleaning supplies next. Next post....do we really need all those specialized cleaners?
